Question
========
Consider a server with one service station and infinite buffer capacity. Measurements give a mean time to answer a request of 20 ms and a variance of 10 ms. The server receives a request every 100 milliseconds on average according to a Poisson distribution.

(a) What is the expected waiting time of the jobs?
(b) What is the expected response time of the server?

Solution
========
Poisson arrivals and a general service time give an M/G/1 queue, so Pollaczek Khinchine applies and needs the second moment.

E[S] = 20 ms, Var(S) = 10, so E[S2] = Var + E[S]^2 = 10 + 400 = 410 ms2.

lambda = 1/100 = 0.01 per ms, so rho = 0.01 x 20 = 0.2.

(a) E[W] = lambda x E[S2] / (2 (1 - rho)) = (0.01 x 410) / (2 x 0.8) = 4.1 / 1.6 = 2.56 ms.

(b) E[R] = E[W] + E[S] = 2.56 + 20 = 22.56 ms.

The classic mistake is to plug the variance directly into the formula instead of the second moment.
